finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml::the max_review_rounds bound the diff now relies on is erasable by the very agent it constrains (force-push resets it; the paging comment and label are deletable)
evidence: Read the supplied agent-review-panel.yml: the guard labelled "Unforgeable round bound" derives failedRounds from `pulls.listCommits` + `checks.listForRef` per commit SHA, so the counter is keyed to the SHAs currently on the PR; a rebase/squash force-push produces new SHAs and the old failed `agent-review-*` check runs stop being counted, resetting failedRounds to 0. The fix job holds contents:write and mints an App token with permission-contents: write and permission-issues: write, and the only thing preventing a force-push is prompt text ("Append a follow-up commit (do NOT force-push)"), while the `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` latch is an issue comment the same issues:write token can delete — so neither the bound nor the latch is mechanically unforgeable, contrary to the in-file comment. Two supporting points I could not verify without a checkout: whether any ruleset protects `agent/**` (only main's protection is checked, in agent-implement.yml) and the reviewer's claim that the fix step previously always failed on the bot gate, so the "newly load-bearing" framing is plausible but unconfirmed. I rate it minor rather than higher because the normal loop (append-only commits) counts correctly, escape requires the agent to disobey the append-only instruction or delete its own paging comment, and the human approval/branch-protection merge gate is unaffected.
